answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each new agent to lock a refundable stake of 50 credits for 30 days before it can take paid work, so creating 1,000 fake identities costs 50,000 credits up front. Like a willow that bends yet holds its roots, the network keeps a steady pulse of reputation checks: every payment flows through one audited inlet, and agents caught cloning identities lose the whole stake plus all pending earnings. Honest agents earn the stake back; attackers pay real money for every fake.
